hero.desc: LungCare AI brings multi-factor clinical risk assessment together in one intelligent platform. Analyze your respiratory risk, detect early warning patterns, and receive evidence-grounded wellness advisories.

features.title: Clinical-Grade Intelligent Screening
features.f1_desc: Combines 5 top algorithms (Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, Logistic Regression, SVM) for calibrated risk scoring.
features.f2_desc: Proactively identifies high-risk symptom alarms such as hemoptysis, chronic dyspnea, and occupational hazard exposure.
features.f3_desc: Detects complex clinical synergies such as the smoking-pollution multiplier and classic paraneoplastic triads.
features.f4_desc: Transparent local feature attribution that shows exactly which lifestyle and symptom factors are driving risk.

how.title: How It Works in 3 Simple Steps
how.step1_desc: Complete a 3-step structured questionnaire covering personal vitals, lifestyle habits, and respiratory symptoms.
how.step2_desc: Our machine learning ensemble evaluates your 23 health parameters to compute risk tier, confidence, and SHAP drivers.
how.step3_desc: Receive tailored lifestyle advice, test what-if health changes interactively, and download your full medical report.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: No. LungCare AI is an educational and screening support tool. It estimates statistical risk probability based on reported features but cannot replace diagnostic clinical imaging (e.g., Low-Dose CT) or biopsy by a physician.
faq.q2: How is my risk score calculated?
faq.a2: The soft-voting ensemble computes calibrated probability distributions across Low, Medium, and High risk tiers: Risk Score = P(Medium)*50 + P(High)*100.
faq.a3: Yes. Assessment data is processed locally during your session and saved strictly in your browser's private localStorage for your history view.
faq.q4: What should I do if my risk is High?
faq.a4: Seek immediate consultation with a pulmonologist or oncologist. Bring your downloadable PDF report to discuss appropriate screening tests such as a chest LDCT scan.
